why: Both operands are `(float)` of the magnitude of a difference of two shorts, so both are exact integers in 0..65535.  |second/nearest - 2| is either 0 -- when second == 2 * nearest -- or at least 1/nearest >= 1/65535 = 1.5e-5, which is ten orders of magnitude above the difference between the two spellings, so only second == 2 * nearest can separate them. Finding F1433.

why: A nearest distance of zero means some k gave |v - linMapp[unSuspectedPhase][from + k]| == 0 and set `bestAt` to that k -- no later k can improve on zero, and nothing writes `linMapp` inside the (code, phase) iteration -- so `linMapp[unSuspectedPhase][bestAt]` still equals `linMapp[phase][at]` at the store and the repair writes the value back over itself. Both outcomes are the same self-store, and neither `second` nor `bestAt` depends on the decision.  Finding F1433.
